intent: The popup of a Select, portalled and positioned against its trigger, that lists the options.
typical_uses: The list of options a SelectTrigger opens

dont_use_when.situation: The list of actions a menu button opens
A list the user filters by typing
A floating panel holding fields, buttons or free-form content

invariants.text: Unless `alignItemWithTrigger` is false, a popup opened by mouse or keyboard overlaps the trigger so the chosen item sits over the trigger's caption, and `side`, `align` and the offsets do not apply; opened by touch, turned off, or short of space, the popup opens on `side` instead.
Children render inside the primitive's listbox list, which the content always places between a SelectScrollUpButton and a SelectScrollDownButton of its own; the list, not the popup, is what scrolls.

Without `container`, the popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.
select.module.css sets the popup's width to the trigger's width (`--anchor-width`) with a 9rem floor, and caps its height at the space available beside the trigger.
The popup fades and scales on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` select.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the default positioning when the trigger sits inside a transformed or filtered container, such as an animated panel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `positionMethod="fixed"`; absolute positioning resolves against the transformed container instead of the page and misplaces the popup

a11y.by: the primitive's Select.List renders role="listbox" (aria-multiselectable under multiple); select.test.tsx asserts no listbox is found while the select is closed and that the listbox is found by its role once open

children.states: children is the popup's rows, the parts listed under accepts
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; an explicit null renders no popup until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between the anchor and the popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus decides where focus goes when the popup closes - true for the default, false for nowhere, a ref, or a function of the interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` mixes a boolean with a ref object and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside SelectContent; only its `container` is exposed, as a prop of the content itself.
Composed inside SelectContent; its placement and collision props are exposed on the content itself.
Composed inside SelectContent as the scrolling listbox that holds the children; it takes no props from the caller.

good.title: A popup opening below the trigger instead of over it
good.code:
<Select items={REGIONS}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Region">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a region" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent alignItemWithTrigger={false} align="start">
    <SelectItem value="eu-central">Frankfurt</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="us-east">Virginia</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

good.title: A popup portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: A made-up position prop on the popup
bad.why: The content takes no `position`; to open the popup on `side` rather than over the trigger, pass `alignItemWithTrigger={false}`.
